chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Ali (peace be upon him) said: "When a man does not impose fasting upon himself as obligatory, then remembers fasting before he eats food or drinks a drink, and has not broken his fast, then he is at his choice: if he wishes, he fasts, and if he wishes, he breaks his fast."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one makes fasting obligatory but forgets the intention before eating?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), citing Imam Ali (AS), clarifies the flexibility in *niyyah* (intention) for voluntary fasting, establishing that the obligation becomes binding only upon the conscious decision to fast. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that if one remembers the fast before consuming food or drink, they retain the option to either complete the fast or break it, emphasizing the role of conscious intent in validating the act of worship. This ruling underscores the importance of *niyyah* as the spiritual foundation of the fast, distinguishing between mere physical abstinence and worshipful observance.
